2: """"
3:     do!(g, v)
4: 
5: Graphical do operator, removes all 
6: incoming edges to vertex `v` in a DiGraph `g`.
7: Returns the modified graph.
8: """
9: function do!(g::DiGraph{T}, v::T) where {T}
10:     for u in collect(inneighbors(g, v))
11:         rem_edge!(g, u, v)
12:     end
13:     return g
14: end

29: Test that given directed graph `g`, no node in `Z` is descendant of `u` and `Z` d-separates `u` from `v` 
30: in the subgraph that only has the backdoors of `u` left (outgoing edges of `u` removed).
31: 
32: If so, the causal effect of `u` on `v` is identifiable and is given by the formula:
33: 
34:     ∑{z∈Z} p(v | u, z)p(z)
35: 
36: In the linear Gaussian model, find `E[Y | X = x, Z = z] = α + βx + γ'z` and obtain `E[Y | do(x)] = α + βx + γ'E[Z].
37: """
38: function backdoor_criterion(g::AbstractGraph{T}, u::Integer, v::Integer, S = T[];
39:                             verbose = false) where {T}
40:     in_seen = falses(nv(g)) # nodes reached earlier backwards
41:     out_seen = falses(nv(g)) # nodes reached earlier forwards
42:     descendant = falses(nv(g)) # descendant in s
43:     blocked = falses(nv(g))
44: 
45:     for ve in S
46:         in_seen[ve] = true
47:         blocked[ve] = true
48:     end
49: 
50:     (in_seen[u] || in_seen[v]) && throw(ArgumentError("S should not contain u or v"))
51: 
52:     u == v && throw(ArgumentError("u == v"))
53: 
54:     next = Vector{T}()
55: 
56:     # mark vertices with descendants in S
57:     next = Vector{T}()
58:     for w in S
59:         push!(next, w)
60:         descendant[w] = true
61:         w == u && return false # u has descendant in S
62:     end
63: 
64:     while !isempty(next)

76:     in_next = Vector{T}()
77:     out_next = Vector{T}()
78: 
79:     push!(in_next, u) # reached u backwards
80:     in_seen[u] = true
81:     out_seen[u] = true
82: 
83:     while true
84:         sin = isempty(in_next)
85:         sout = isempty(out_next)
86:         sin && sout && return true # no vertices in the queue
87: 
88:         if !sin # some vertex reach backwards in the queue
89:             src = popfirst!(in_next)
90:             src != u && for w in outneighbors(g, src) # possible collider at destination
91:                 if !out_seen[w] && (!blocked[w] || descendant[w])
92:                     verbose && println("<- $src -> $w")
93:                     w == v && return false
94:                     push!(out_next, w)
95:                     out_seen[w] = true
96:                 end
97:             end
98:             for w in inneighbors(g, src)
99:                 if !in_seen[w]
100:                     verbose && println("<- $src <- $w")
101:                     w == v && return false
102:                     push!(in_next, w)
103:                     in_seen[w] = true
104:                 end
105:             end
106:         end
107:         if !sout # some vertex reach forwards in the queue
108:             src = popfirst!(out_next)
109:             for w in outneighbors(g, src) # possible collider at destination
110:                 if !out_seen[w] && !blocked[src] && (!blocked[w] || descendant[w])
111:                     verbose && println("-> $src -> $w")
112:                     w == v && return false
113:                     push!(out_next, w)
114:                     out_seen[w] = true
115:                 end
116:             end
117:             for w in inneighbors(g, src) # collider at source
118:                 if !in_seen[w] && descendant[src] # shielded collider
119:                     verbose && println("-> $src <- $w")
120:                     w == v && return false
121:                     push!(out_next, w)
122:                     in_seen[w] = true
123:                 end
124:             end
125:         end
126:     end
127: end

3: """
4:     has_recanting_witness(g::AbstractGraph, u, v,  blocked_edges::AbstractGraph) -> Bool
5: 
6: In a causal DAG with edges `g`, determine whether path-specific causal effect from vertex `u` to `v`
7: with edges in `blocked_edges` blocked can be can be computed uniquely from the data available to the investigator (assuming complete observations),
8: which is the case if there is no "recanting witness".
9: Essentially this means that `blocked_edges` could equivalently be replaced by a blocking only
10: outgoing edges of `u`. 
11: 
12: See Alvin, Shpitser, Pearl (2005): "Identifiability of Path-Specific Effects", 
13: https://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/r321-L.pdf.    
14: """
15: function has_recanting_witness(g::AbstractGraph{T}, u::Integer, v::Integer,
16:                                blocked_edges::AbstractGraph{T}) where {T}
17:     on_blocked = zeros(Bool, nv(g))
18:     on_open = zeros(Bool, nv(g))
19:     may_blocked = zeros(Bool, nv(g))
20:     for e in edges(blocked_edges) # mark sources of blocked edges
21:         may_blocked[src(e)] = true
22:     end
23:     u == v && error("u == v")
24: 
25:     for nbr in outneighbors(g, u) # if there is a recanting witness, a neighbour of u is one too
26:         on_blocked .= false
27:         on_open .= false
28:         may_blocked[v] && has_edge(blocked_edges, v, nbr) && continue
29:         nbr == v && continue # direct edge
30: 
31:         next_open = Vector{T}()
32:         next_blocked = Vector{T}()
33: 
34:         push!(next_open, nbr)
35:         on_open[nbr] = true
36:         while !isempty(next_open) # find all reachable via direct neighbour
37:             src = popfirst!(next_open) # get new element from queue
38:             for vertex in outneighbors(g, src)
39:                 if may_blocked[src] && has_edge(blocked_edges, src, vertex)
40:                     if !on_blocked[vertex]
41:                         on_blocked[vertex] = true
42:                         if vertex != v
43:                             push!(next_blocked, vertex)  # push onto blocked queue
44:                         end
45:                     end
46:                 elseif !on_open[vertex]
47:                     on_open[vertex] = true
48:                     if vertex != v
49:                         push!(next_open, vertex) # push onto queue
50:                     end
51:                 end
52:             end
53:         end
54:         while !isempty(next_blocked) # find all reachable through the blocked edge
55:             src = popfirst!(next_blocked) # get new element from queue
56:             for vertex in outneighbors(g, src)
57:                 if !on_blocked[vertex]
58:                     on_blocked[vertex] = true
59:                     if vertex != v
60:                         push!(next_blocked, vertex)  # push onto blocked queue
61:                     end
62:                 end
63:             end
64:         end
65:         if on_blocked[v] && on_open[v]
66:             return true
67:         end
68:     end
69:     return false
70: end

31: 
32: We are interested in the average causal effect (ACE) of a treatment `X` (variable nr. 6) on an outcome `Y` (variable nr.  8), which stands for the expected increase of `Y` per unit of a controlled increase in `X`. Variables nr. 1 and nr. 2 are unobserved.
33: 
34: *Regressing `Y` (nr. 8) on `X` (nr. 6) will fail to measure the effect because of the presence of a confounder `C` (variable nr.  4)*, which opens a backdoor path, a connection between `X` and `Y` via the path 6 ← 4 → 8 which is not causal. 
35: 
36: ![Confounder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mschauer/CausalInference.jl/master/assets/backdoor1.png)
37: 
38: 
39: We can avert such problems by checking the backdoor criterion. Indeed
40: ```julia
41: backdoor_criterion(dag, 6, 8) # false
42: ```
43: reports a problem.
44: 
45: One might want to condition on the confounder `C` (nr. 4)` to obtain the causal effect,
46: but then  
47: ```julia
48: backdoor_criterion(dag, 6, 8, [4]) # still false
49: ```
50: there is still a problem ( 
51: because that conditioning opens up a non-causal path via 6 ← 3 ← 1 → 4 ← 2 → 5 → 8.)
52: 
53: ![Opened new path](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mschauer/CausalInference.jl/master/assets/backdoor2.png)
54: 
55: 
56: But conditioning on both `Z = [4, 5]` solves the problem, as verified by the backdoor criterion.
57: ```julia
58: backdoor_criterion(dag, 6, 8, [3, 4]) # true
59: backdoor_criterion(dag, 6, 8, [4, 5]) # true
60: ```
61: (also conditioning on `Z = [3, 4]` would be possible.)
62: 
63: Thus, regressing `Y` on `X` and controlling for variables numbered `Z = [4, 5]` we measure the average causal effect.
64: 
65: ![Good controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mschauer/CausalInference.jl/master/assets/backdoor3.png)
66: 
67: What we have done by hand here is the search for an backdoor adjustment set. We could have directly queried
68: ```julia
69: Zs = list_covariate_adjustment(dag, 6, 8, Int[], setdiff(Set(1:8), [1, 2])) # exclude variables nr. 1 and nr. 2 because they are unobserved.
70: ```
71: which lists possible adjustment sets,
72: ```julia
73: println.(Zs);
74: ```
75: ```
76:     Set([4, 3])
77:     Set([5, 4])
78:     Set([5, 4, 3])
79: ```
80: to get the list of possible adjustment sets. Here `list_backdoor_adjustment` gives adjustment sets for a backdoor criterion similar to `backdoor_criterion` and `list_covariate_adjustment` the more versatile adjustment set 
81: based on the sound and complete graphical criterion for
82: covariate adjustment given in [https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3515]
83: using the algorithmic approach proposed in
84: [https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.00116].

118: """
119:     test_covariate_adjustment(g, X, Y, S)
120: 
121: Check if `S` is a covariate adjustment set relative to `(X, Y)` in graph `g`. 
122: 
123: Based on the sound and complete graphical criterion for covariate adjustment given in https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3515 using the algorithmic approach proposed in https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.00116. Output is a boolean.
124: """
125: function test_covariate_adjustment(g, X, Y, S)
126:     X, Y, S = toset.((X, Y, S))
127:     PCPXY = pcp(g, X, Y)
128:     length(intersect(S, descendants(g, PCPXY))) != 0 && return false
129:     return alt_test_dsep(g, X, Y, S, (pe, ne, v, w) -> v in X && w in PCPXY && ne == RIGHT)
130: end
131: 
132: """
133:     alt_test_backdoor(g, X, Y, S)
134: 
135: Check if `S` satisfies the backdoor criterion relative to `(X, Y)` in graph `g`. 
136: 
137: The generalization to sets X and Y differs from, e.g., Pearl (2009). See the Example section (TODO: ref).
138: """
139: function alt_test_backdoor(g, X, Y, S)
140:     X, Y, S = toset.((X, Y, S))
141:     length(intersect(S, descendants(g, X))) != 0 && return false
142:     return alt_test_dsep(g, X, Y, S, no_outgoing(X))
143: end

145: """
146:     find_dsep(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y), veto = no_veto)
147: 
148: Find a d-separator `Z` with ``I ⊆ Z ⊆ R`` for sets of vertices `X` and `Y` in `g`, else return `false`. 
149: 
150: Based on the algorithmic approach proposed in https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.00116. 
151: """
152: function find_dsep(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y), veto = no_veto)
153:     X, Y, I, R = toset.((X, Y, I, R))
154:     Z = intersect(R, setdiff(ancestors(g, union(X, Y, I), veto), X, Y))
155:     if alt_test_dsep(g, X, Y, Z, veto)
156:         return Z
157:     else
158:         return false
159:     end
160: end

187: """
188:     find_covariate_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
189: 
190: Find a covariate adjustment set `Z` with ``I ⊆ Z ⊆ R`` for sets of vertices `X` and `Y` in `g`, else return `false`. 
191: 
192: Based on the algorithmic approach proposed in https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.00116. 
193: """
194: function find_covariate_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
195:     X, Y, I, R = toset.((X, Y, I, R))
196:     PCPXY = pcp(g, X, Y)
197:     Z = setdiff(intersect(ancestors(g, union(X, Y, I)), R), X, Y, descendants(g, PCPXY))
198:     if issubset(I, Z) && alt_test_dsep(g, X, Y, Z, (pe, ne, v, w) -> v in X && w in PCPXY && ne == RIGHT)
199:         return Z
200:     else
201:         return false
202:     end
203: end
204: 
205: """
206:     find_backdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
207: 
208: Find a backdoor adjustment set `Z` with ``I ⊆ Z ⊆ R`` for sets of vertices `X` and `Y` in `g`, else return `false`. 
209: 
210: The generalization to sets X and Y differs from, e.g., Pearl (2009). See the Example section (TODO: ref).
211: """
212: function find_backdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
213:     (X, Y, I, R) = toset.((X, Y, I, R))
214:     bdZ = setdiff(find_covariate_adjustment(g, X, Y, I, R), descendants(g, X, no_incoming(X)))
215:     # we generalize bd to sets by testing (X indep Y given Z) in G with outgoing edges from X removed
216:     # instead of checking the bd criterion for pairs of vertices (x in X and y in Y) as originally proposed by Pearl which is more restrictive
217:     if issubset(I, bdZ) && alt_test_dsep(g, X, Y, bdZ, no_outgoing(X))
218:         return bdZ
219:     else
220:         return false
221:     end
222: end

224: """
225:     find_min_covariate_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
226: 
227: Find an inclusion minimal covariate adjustment set `Z` with ``I ⊆ Z ⊆ R`` for sets of vertices `X` and `Y` in `g`, else return `false`. 
228: 
229: Based on the algorithmic approach proposed in https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.00116.  
230: """
231: function find_min_covariate_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
232:     X, Y, I, R = toset.((X, Y, I, R))
233:     PCPXY = pcp(g, X, Y)    
234:     return find_min_dsep(g, X, Y, I, setdiff(R, descendants(g, PCPXY)), (pe, ne, v, w) -> v in X && w in PCPXY && ne == RIGHT)
235: end

237: """
238:     find_min_backdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
239: 
240: Find an inclusion minimal backdoor adjustment set `Z` with ``I ⊆ Z ⊆ R`` for sets of vertices `X` and `Y` in `g`, else return `false`. 
241: 
242: The generalization to sets X and Y differs from, e.g., Pearl (2009). See the Example section (TODO: ref).
243: """
244: function find_min_backdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
245:     X, Y, I, R = toset.((X, Y, I, R))
246:     return find_min_dsep(g, X, Y, I, setdiff(R, descendants(g, X)), (pe, ne, v, w) -> v in X && ne == RIGHT)

249: """
250:     find_frontdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
251: 
252: Find a frontdoor adjustment set `Z` with ``I ⊆ Z ⊆ R`` for sets of vertices `X` and `Y` in `g`, else return `false`. 
253: 
254: Based on the algorithm given in  https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16468. 
255: """
256: function find_frontdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
257:     X, Y, I, R = toset.((X, Y, I, R))
258:     Za = setdiff(R, bayesball(g, X, Set{Integer}(), no_outgoing(X)))
259:     A = ancestors(g, Y)
260:     function Zab_pass(pe, ne, v, w)
261:         v in X && return false
262:         ne == RIGHT && return true
263:         pe == RIGHT && v in A && !(w in Za) && return true
264:         (pe == INIT || pe == LEFT) && !(w in Za) && return true
265:         return false
266:     end
267:     Zab = setdiff(Za, gensearch(g, Y, Zab_pass))
268:     if issubset(I, Zab) && length(intersect(descendants(g, X, no_outgoing(Zab)), Y)) == 0
269:         return Zab
270:     else
271:         return false
272:     end
273: end
274: 
275: """
276:     find_min_frontdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
277: 
278: Find an inclusion minimal frontdoor adjustment set `Z` with ``I ⊆ Z ⊆ R`` for sets of vertices `X` and `Y` in `g`, else returns `false`. 
279: 
280: Based on the algorithm given in https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16468. 
281: """
282: function find_min_frontdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I = Set{eltype(g)}(), R = setdiff(Set(vertices(g)), X, Y))
283:     X, Y, I, R = toset.((X, Y, I, R))
284:     # write explanation for the pass rules
285:     Zii = find_frontdoor_adjustment(g, X, Y, I, R)
286:     Zii == false && return false 
287:     function Za_pass(pe, ne, v, w)
288:         pe in [INIT, LEFT] && ne == LEFT && !(v in Zii) && !inunion(w, X, Y) && return true
289:         return false
290:     end
291:     Za = intersect(gensearch(g, Y, Za_pass), Zii) 
292:     function Zxy_pass(pe, ne, v, w)
293:         pe in [INIT, RIGHT] && ne == RIGHT && !(v in Za) && !inunion(w, X, Y, I) && return true
294:         return false
295:     end
296:     Zxy = intersect(gensearch(g, X, Zxy_pass), Za)
297:     function Zzy_pass(pe, ne, v, w)
298:         pe in [INIT, LEFT] && ne == LEFT && !inunion(w, X, I, Zxy) && return true
299:         pe in [LEFT, RIGHT] && ne == RIGHT && !(w in X) && !inunion(v, I, Za) && return true
300:         pe == RIGHT && ne == LEFT && inunion(v, I, Za) && !inunion(w, X, I, Zxy) && return true
301:         return false
302:     end
303:     Zzy = intersect(gensearch(g, union(I, Zxy), Zzy_pass), Za) 
304:     return union(I, Zxy, Zzy)
305: end

316: function downwards(state, I, R)
317:     v = first(setdiff(R, I))
318:     push!(state, (:up, :I, v, I, R))
319:     push!(state, (:down, :I, v, I, R))
320:     push!(state, (:up, :R, v, I, R))
321:     push!(state, (:down, :R, v, I, R))
322: end

324: function Base.iterate(A::ConstraintIterator)
325:     R = deepcopy(A.R)
326:     I = deepcopy(A.I)
327:     state = Vector{Tuple{Symbol, Symbol, eltype(A.g), Set{eltype(A.g)}, Set{eltype(A.g)}}}()
328:     A.find(A.g, A.X, A.Y, I, R) == false && return nothing
329:     issetequal(I, R) && return I, state
330:     downwards(state, I, R)
331:     Base.iterate(A, state)
332: end
333: 
334: function Base.iterate(A::ConstraintIterator, state)
335:     while !isempty(state)
336:         dir, set, v, I, R = pop!(state)
337:         dir == :down && set == :I && push!(I, v)
338:         dir == :up && set == :I && delete!(I, v)
339:         dir == :down && set == :R && delete!(R, v)
340:         dir == :up && set == :R && push!(R, v)
341:         A.find(A.g,  A.X, A.Y, I, R) == false && continue
342:         issetequal(I, R) && return deepcopy(I), state
343:         if dir == :down
344:             downwards(state, I, R)
345:         end
346:     end
347:     return nothing
348: end

465: 	listMsasTotalEffect : function( g, M, F, max_nr ){
466: 		var gtype = g.getType()
467: 		if( gtype != "dag" && gtype != "pdag" && gtype != "mag" && gtype != "pag" ){
468: 			throw( "Cannot compute total affect adjustment sets for graph of type "+gtype )
469: 		}
470: 
471: 		if( !g || g.getSources().length < 1 || g.getTargets().length < 1 ){ return [] }
472: 
473: 		var gg = g
474: 		if( gtype == "pdag" ){
475: 			gg = GraphTransformer.cgToRcg( g )
476: 		}
477: 		if( M ){
478: 			_.each( M, function(v){ gg.addAdjustedNode( v ) } )
479: 		}
480: 		if( F ){
481: 			_.each( F, function(v){ gg.addLatentNode( v ) } )
482: 		}
483: 	
484: 
485: 		if( GraphAnalyzer.violatesAdjustmentCriterion(gg)){ return [] }
486: 		
487: 		var gbd = GraphTransformer.backDoorGraph(gg)
488: 		var S = gg.getSelectedNodes()
489: 		if( S.length > 0 ){
490: 			if( this.dConnected( gbd, gbd.getTargets(), _.map(S, Graph.getVertex, gbd ) ) ){
491: 				return []
492: 			} else {
493: 				_.each( S, function(s){ gbd.removeSelectedNode( s ); gbd.addAdjustedNode( s ) } )			
494: 			}
495: 		}
496: 
497: 		var gam = GraphTransformer.moralGraph( GraphTransformer.ancestorGraph( gbd ) )
498: 
499: 		var adjusted_nodes = _.map( gg.getAdjustedNodes(), Graph.getVertex, gam )
500: 		var latent_nodes = _.map( gg.getLatentNodes().concat( this.dpcp(gg) ), Graph.getVertex, gam )
501: 
502: 		// at this point, "latent_nodes" may contain 
503: 		// undefined values because not all adjusted or latent nodes may have beeen
504: 		// retained in the moral graph. Therefore, we use "compact" to remove such
505: 		// values. 
506: 		var r = this.listMinimalSeparators( gam, 
507: 			adjusted_nodes, 
508: 			_.compact(latent_nodes), max_nr )
509: 
510: 		// Give back vertex objects from original graph, rather than the constructed 
511: 		// ancestor moral graph.
512: 		S = _.map( S, Graph.getVertex, g )
513: 		for( i = 0 ; i < r.length ; i ++ ){
514: 			r[i] = _.map( r[i], Graph.getVertex, g )
515: 			r[i] = _.difference( r[i], S )
516: 		}
517: 		return r
518: 	},
